schemaNote: Each entry is keyed as "<year>|<company name as in companies.json>" and holds an array of individually-sourced facts. A fact is only added when a specific field (founders, funding, investors, geography, status) is confirmed by a named primary source: the company's own site or press release, an investor's press release, an official STATION F publication, or a relevant government registry. LinkedIn, Crunchbase, other aggregators, or inference are never used as the sole evidence for a fact. For field "status", value must start with one of "Active", "Acquired", "Closed", "Rebranded", "Dormant" (optionally followed by ": short detail") so the site can render the correct status pill; verifiedAt records the date the status was checked, not a permanent fact — a status can go stale and should be re-verified periodically. "Rebranded" is for a company still operating as the same team/entity under a new name/domain (confirmed by the company's own site, app-store listing, or press release saying so) — it is distinct from "Acquired" (bought by someone else) and "Closed" (shut down). "Dormant" is different from all four: it does NOT claim to know the company's fate. It means a specific check (company registry search, archive.org snapshot history) found no sign of activity after a given year and no record of acquisition, closure or rebrand either — an honest "we looked and found nothing past this point", not a guess that the company is closed. Its source must be the specific registry/archive query that came up empty (e.g. a BODACC or Pappers search, or a Wayback Machine capture history), not just "no news found" from a general web search.
